convention: inputs f32 (exact in JSON); expected f64 math on those inputs, except fields named *_f32 and the rope block (f32 pipeline)

hc_mix.note: row 1 is row-scaled x100 inside x: mixes are scale-invariant up to the eps

router.note: row 2: experts 100..119 share one score and zero bias, so ids are 100..115 (ties to lowest); rows 0/1 have a k-th margin far above f32 sigmoid noise

engram_block.layout: rows [n, n_cols, head_dim]; lookup_norm [n_cols, head_dim] (GGUF ggml [head_dim, n_cols]); kv_w [(hc+1)*d, n_cols*head_dim] row-major out x in (keys c=0..hc-1 then value); kv_b [(hc+1), d]; gate_w / hc_scale [hc, d]; pre_gamma [d]

kpool_pool_score.layout: wv / wg [out, in]; ape [slot, head_dim] (GGUF ggml [head_dim, 4]); iq [t, heads, head_dim] before rope; rope on dims 64..127, pooled key at its group's first position 4g, query at t
kpool_pool_score.note: score[t][g] is null where g >= t//4 (own group and later are never scored); tokens 8, 9 are an open group: not pooled

kpool_select.note: integer scores 0..63 give many ties: ranking is score desc then group id asc; a query with t < 2048 sees every earlier cell; n_cells <= 511*4 + 4
